newsitem.title: CANADA: Goodale sees CWB barley plebiscite by February '97.
newsitem.headline: Goodale sees CWB barley plebiscite by February '97.

text.p: A Prairie-wide farmer plebiscite on whether the Canadian Wheat Board should retain its barley export monopoly would likely be held by February, Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale said.
"I would think January, February is the logical period. I wouldn't want to delay beyond February and interfere with spring seeding," Goodale told reporters in a conference call.
Goodale said Friday he is considering holding a referendum on what has become the most controversial CWB issue.
A panel appointed by Goodale suggested ending the CWB feed barley monopoly.
The 61-year-old state commodity trading agency is one of the world's oldest and largest such monopolies.
"With those results we could move by the beginning of the next crop year," Goodale said.
The CWB held a 48 percent share of world malting barley exports and 11 percent of feed barley world market share in marketing year 1994/95 (Aug/July).

Canada produced 11.7 million tonnes of all types of barley in 1994/95 and exported 3.5 million tonnes, or 30 percent, all through the CWB, Agriculture Canada and CWB figures show. Asked whether a majority vote would be sufficient to determine the course of feed and malt barley marketing, Goodale said, "Suppose there's a lopsided result but only 25 percent of voters turn out. I would have to question whether that's a representative result."
